descriptionChirho: To move unsteadily back and forth, swaying like a drunkard, a reed in the wind, or the earth in an earthquake. Qal intransitive and Niphal: the trees of the forest swaying (Judg 9:9, 11, 13), Hannah's lips moving in prayer (1 Sam 1:13), the earth staggering like a drunkard (Isa 24:20), staggering from wine (Isa 29:9), mountains being shaken (Nah 3:12), doorposts shaking (Isa 6:4), and pendulous objects swinging (Job 28:4). Includes the Niphal passive 'be shaken'. Multilingual glosses confirm: Ar. tatamayalu/tarannahhu, Ger. wankt/bewegen, Sp. se tambaleaban/se mece, Hin. hilte/dagmagaate, Kor. heundeullida.

Hiphil causative: to shake or wag something deliberately, especially the head in mockery or scorn, or to cause someone to tremble. Used of the daughter of Zion wagging her head at the Assyrians (2 Kgs 19:21; Isa 37:22), of enemies shaking their heads in derision (Ps 22:7; 109:25; Lam 2:15), of Job proposing to shake his head in comfort (Job 16:4), of Zephaniah's prophecy that passersby will shake their fist (Zeph 2:15), of a king moving his troops (2 Kgs 23:18), and of the angel setting Daniel trembling (Dan 10:10). Glosses: Ar. hazzat/yuhanghighuna, Ger. wankte, Sp. meneo/agitara, Hin. hilate hain, Kor. heundeulda.

To move about aimlessly without a fixed dwelling, as a vagabond, exile, or refugee. Qal intransitive: Cain condemned to be a wanderer (na') on the earth (Gen 4:12, 14), the psalmist's imprecation that enemies wander and beg (Ps 59:15; 109:10), the blind wandering in the streets of Jerusalem (Lam 4:14-15), people roaming sea to sea seeking God's word (Amos 8:12), and Judah's idols staggering about without direction (Jer 14:10). The 'wandering' sense is distinct from mere physical swaying in that it involves displacement and homelessness. Glosses: Ar. ta'ihan, Ger. unstet, Sp. errante/vagaron, Hin. bhatakta, Kor. yurihaneun/bangwanghara.

Hiphil causative of the wandering sense: to make someone roam as a fugitive or to scatter them abroad. Used of YHWH making Israel wander in the wilderness for forty years (Num 32:13), of the psalmist praying for God to scatter his enemies and make them wander (Ps 59:11), and of Jeremiah's question about causing displacement (2 Sam 15:20 ketiv/qere). The causative adds an agent who forces the wandering upon another. Glosses: Ar. fa-atahahum, Eng. made them wander/shall I make you wander, Sp. los hizo vagar, Hin. bhatakaya, Kor. bangwanghage hasyeotda.

To shake or shudder involuntarily from fear, awe, or seismic disturbance. Qal intransitive: the people trembled at Sinai when they saw the thunder and lightning (Exod 20:18), Ahaz's heart and his people trembled like trees of the forest before the wind (Isa 7:2), idolaters will tremble before YHWH (Isa 19:1). Distinguished from 'stagger/sway' by the emotional cause (fear/awe) and from 'wander' by being involuntary physical response rather than displacement. Glosses: Ar. irta'adu/tazaz'azu, Sp. temblaron/temblaran, Hin. kampe/kaampenge, Kor. tteollyeotdoda.

labelChirho: sift, shake out as in a sieve
descriptionChirho: To shake back and forth as grain in a sieve, to sift or winnow by shaking -- a metaphorical extension of the physical shaking sense applied to divine judgment. Used in Amos 9:9 where YHWH says he will sift (wa-hanhi'othi) the house of Israel among the nations as grain is shaken (yinnoa') in a sieve. The Hiphil/Niphal combination conveys both the divine agent doing the shaking and the grain being shaken. Glosses: Ar. ugharbilu 'I will sift', Eng. I will shake / is shaken, Sp. sacudire/se sacude, Hin. chanunga/chhana jata hai, Kor. heundeullira.
